To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the Ca2+ influx induced by histamine is regulated by the membrane potential, whereas the Ca2+-influx induced by TG is regulated by both the membrane potential and the refilling state, 2) TG pretreatment modifies IP3 metabolism by reducing the IP2 level and increasing the IP1 level, and 3) the Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release mechanism is not involved in the Ca2+ signal induced by histamine.

(i) the refilling state is not the only signal controlling Ca2+ influx; and (ii) histamine and thapsigargin seem to activate Ca(2+)-influx through distinct but interrelated pathways regulated by the membrane potential.
the refilling status of internal Ca2 stores does not constitute a unique regulator of Ca2 influx in human endothelium.

the refilling level of the internal Ca2+ pool regulates the Ca2+ influx by a direct action on the plasma membrane Ca2+ channel, but also indirectly by modulating the membrane potential and the Ca2+ channel activity.
